pending_items.title: Socialist weather and dogs barking in Hebrew: America's Thanksgiving culture wars
pending_items.content:
Americans celebrating Thanksgiving this year have been presented with two rather unexpected political developments: New York City's Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani now has control over the weather, and US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee's dogs may have acquired a second language.

While millions of Americans gathered with their families on Thursday, social media users were engaged in another traditional Thanksgiving activity: fighting over politics. But this time it was socialism, Islam and Zionism that took centre stage in this debate.

The postponement of NYC's iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade because of severe weather conditions sent right-wing commentators into a frenzy, with some suggesting the decision had less to do with meteorology and more to do with Mamdani's political and religious affiliations.

It appears that, in addition to affordable housing, universal childcare and free buses, Mamdani's socialist agenda has taken over the weather in Manhattan.

Some users shared live webcam footage of Times Square in an apparent attempt to discredit weather forecasts, while others suggested that New Yorkers had been duped into believing the parade was called off because of rain.

For others, the mayor's Democratic Socialist background offered an alternate explanation for the storm ripping through New York.

Never mind that the parade has not actually been cancelled, but postponed until Saturday.

Gotta hand it to Mamdani. The guy killed the New York City Thanksgiving Parade for the first time in 100 years, and everyone is walking around believing that it has to do with rain.

Unfortunately for proponents of the weather conspiracy, New York's precautions surrounding parade balloons considerably predate Mamdani's political career.

In 1997, strong winds caused a giant Cat in the Hat balloon to strike a lamppost, seriously injuring a spectator.

The following year, the city introduced safety regulations limiting balloon operations to sustained winds of 23mph (37kmph) and gusts of 34mph - well below the gusts of up to 65mph forecast for Thanksgiving.

The mayor responsible for introducing those measures was Republican Rudy Giuliani, which makes social media reactions like the X post depicting “the last Republican in NYC” all the more bizarre.

🇺🇸 The last republican in NYC, standing in front of Mamdani's Thanksgiving parade. One man, no tanks needed, just a mayor who postponed 100 years of tradition. #MamdaniOutNow #HappyThanksgiving https://t.co/qvnMANJmZe

Philadelphia also disrupted its Thanksgiving festivities due to severe weather.

Meanwhile, thousands of miles away, a prominent figure on the Christian-Zionist right was celebrating Thanksgiving from Israel.

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee appeared alongside his wife and their two dogs in a video expressing gratitude for the opportunity to live in the biblical land.

"What an amazing privilege it is to live here at such a consequential time. And one thing is for sure, it's never boring," Huckabee said, in a particularly jarring choice of words against the backdrop of Israel's genocide in Gaza.

One user on Reddit wrote , “Never boring? Yeah, because they keep killing innocent people. They get the thrill from it.”

But the longtime supporter of Israel had another important development to share.

"Our dogs like it too, in fact, we think they now are barking in Hebrew."

The announcement left some on social media questioning whether the video was even real.

Others wondered how Huckabee's effusive praise for Israel squared with the Trump administration's much-touted "America First" agenda.

@USAmbIsrael Imagine an American sending a message on a uniquely American holiday and using it to praise Israel.

And so, this Thanksgiving, Americans found themselves debating the political affiliations of a weather forecast and the linguistic capabilities of two dogs.

The turkeys, at least, were largely spared the culture wars.

pending_items.title: Attack on Saudi’s Jazan refinery kills one person, disrupts operations
pending_items.content:
An aerial projectile has hit an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s city of Jazan, killing one worker and injuring several other people, according to the country’s Ministry of Energy.

Thursday’s attack on the facility on the kingdom’s Red Sea coast caused a fire and temporarily halted some operations, the ministry said.

The statement did not identify who carried out the strike, but earlier the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said that the Iranian-backed group had ⁠⁠attacked the refinery. It came after Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency had issued an alert about potential danger in Jazan province.

The strike was the Houthis ‘ latest blow against key Saudi facilities, a day after the group claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom’s largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, amid escalating hostilities between the two sides.

The Saudi Ministry of Energy said the worker who died was Nepali, while the injured were of various nationalities.

The injured received medical care, while emergency personnel and specialised technical teams arrived at the site to assess the damage and verify the safety of the facilities following the attack, the ministry added.

The refinery in southwestern Saudi Arabia , near the Yemeni border, is designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day.

The Saudi-led coalition, which is backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its fight with the Houthis, condemned the strike and threatened a counterattack.

“Targeting civilians and ⁠⁠civilian infrastructure would ⁠⁠be ⁠⁠met with a firm military ‌‌response,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki posted on X.

Later on Thursday, the coalition claimed its forces had destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launch platform in Yemen’s Hodeidah governorate used by the armed group to stage the attack on the Jazan refinery, according to al-Maliki. There was no immediate statement from the Houthis regarding the strike.

On the ground in Yemen, meanwhile, Saudi-backed government forces claimed they had carried out 767 strikes on Houthi positions on Thursday.

In a post on X, the forces’ spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said the strikes had “neutralised” 117 Houthi fighters and destroyed 87 vehicles and combat assets.

Al-Nuzaili added that government forces continued to confront Houthi formations on the front lines in northern and western Marib governorate, as well as in the governorates of al-Jawf, Taiz, Lahj, Shabwah and Hajjah.

Earlier on Thursday, a series of air strikes targeted Yemen’s Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, according to media affiliated with the armed group, which is also known as Ansar Allah – Arabic for Supporters of God.

Elsewhere, Houthi forces targeted Habib al-Sarm and al-Hujalla, as well as al-Aqroud in al-Masrakh district.

The Houthis, who control the most populous areas of Yemen, have launched missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings since the country’s civil war reignited in July, in a spillover from the US-Iran war.

The attacks have previously temporarily disrupted some of Aramco’s operations and caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh. They also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including football’s AFC Asian Cup and the flagship FII investment conference.

The fighting has also exacerbated dire humanitarian conditions for Yemeni civilians.

The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that as of Monday, 2,361 people had been killed and 10,982 injured since fighting in Yemen escalated in August. More than 360,000 people have also been forced to flee their homes in Yemen since the start of August, according to the UN.
